items.title: Finder preview and icon caches
items.reason: No sandbox-safe, user-approved cache refresh operation is implemented.
items.operation: Refresh Quick Look and icon services, then move only the three named user cache directories to Trash.
items.threat: Refreshing services or moving an active cache can disrupt Finder previews and recreate data while it is inspected.
items.recovery: Trash Put Back may restore moved cache files; macOS can regenerate caches, but prior thumbnails and timing are not guaranteed.

items.title: Saved application state
items.reason: A design contract exists, but native preview, running-app guards and Trash execution are not implemented.
items.operation: Move explicitly selected, old application saved-state bundles to Trash after checking the owning app is closed.
items.threat: An active app can rewrite its saved state; removal loses window and resume state.
items.recovery: Finder Put Back is possible while the bundle remains in Trash; emptied Trash cannot restore prior window state.

items.title: Damaged application preferences
items.reason: No attributed preference-file preview or safe native effect is implemented.
items.operation: Lint and individually select damaged third-party preference plists under an authorized user directory, then move them to Trash.
items.threat: A failed lint is not proof that an application's preference is disposable; moving it resets settings and may race a running app.
items.recovery: Put Back can restore the exact original file before Trash is emptied, but later app writes may conflict.

items.title: Mail, Messages and Safari databases
items.reason: Protected application databases and live-writer coordination cannot be safely handled in this sandboxed App.
items.operation: After an integrity check and verified closed-owner state, VACUUM each explicitly selected database with a bounded native operation.
items.threat: A locked or live database, WAL companions, insufficient free space or an interrupted rewrite can corrupt user history or messages.
items.recovery: Requires a verified same-snapshot backup and an owner-specific restore procedure; no such recovery path is implemented.

items.title: Download quarantine history
items.reason: The Gatekeeper history database is protected user metadata and no safe per-record preview or restore path is implemented.
items.operation: Delete selected records from the user's QuarantineEventsV2 database and compact it without changing per-file quarantine flags.
items.threat: Clearing download provenance is privacy-sensitive and a live database rewrite can lose or corrupt metadata.
items.recovery: Would require a verified database backup and exact restore with the owning service stopped; currently unavailable.

items.title: Shared file lists
items.reason: No native ownership, format and active-service checks exist for shared file-list files.
items.operation: Inspect selected .sfl2/.sfl3 files while excluding recent-document lists; move only proven damaged files to Trash.
items.threat: A malformed-file heuristic can discard Dock, Finder or application lists that are still useful or actively written.
items.recovery: Put Back can restore the moved file before Trash is emptied; list ordering and service state may not return automatically.

items.title: User Launch Agents
items.reason: A missing executable does not by itself prove an agent is obsolete; no owner-aware admission and rollback are implemented.
items.operation: Inspect selected user LaunchAgent plists and their executable paths, then disable and move only proven orphaned plists to Trash.
items.threat: Network volumes can be temporarily unmounted, and disabling a legitimate agent can stop sync or security software.
items.recovery: Put Back restores the plist while it remains in Trash; re-enabling its launchd service is a separate explicit step.

items.title: Notification history
items.reason: The live Notification Center database is service-owned and not available for safe mutation in this sandbox.
items.operation: Select old delivered records in the user notification database and compact the database after its owner is closed.
items.threat: A concurrent notification writer or schema change can lose notifications or damage the database.
items.recovery: Would require a verified database backup and service-aware restore; no such path exists.

items.title: Knowledge usage database
items.reason: The Knowledge database is service-owned, and safe sandbox access, snapshot and restore are unproven.
items.operation: Inspect the user Knowledge database and WAL companions, then compact or retire only explicitly approved data.
items.threat: Removing WAL/SHM files or rewriting an active database can lose usage history and corrupt its next opening.
items.recovery: Would require a consistent database snapshot and service-aware restore; no such path exists.
